pulls.title: 8393338: C2: Out-of-bounds constant VectorSlice index crashes x86 code generation
pulls.author: jatin-bhateja
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi All, Currently, the constant-index slice inline expander did not check that the origin was in range. Java calls checkIndex before the slice intrinsic, and the first interpreter invocation throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. When compiled with -Xcomp, C2 compiles the method immediately, intrinsifies the out-of-range constant, and crashes in the assembler instead of throwing. This patch adds relevant check in inline expander which now accepts only origins in [0, length]. Kindly review and share your feedback. pulls.title: 8393533: RISC-V: C2: Eliminate redundant vsetvli instructions
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: C2 currently emits RVV configuration code independently for vector instructions. This can produce redundant vsetvli/vsetivli instructions when consecutive operations require the same vector configuration. This change introduces a conservative, extended-basic-block-local optimization after register allocation. It tracks the (SEW, VL) configuration established by supported unmasked vector operations, including loads and stores, and omits redundant configuration code. The configuration can be reused across scalar instructions that preserve VL and VTYPE, as well as across single-predecessor block

pulls.title: 8389239: RISC-V: Optimize copy_memory_v by reducing LMUL and hoisting vsetvli out of loop
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, this patch optimizes copy_memory_v to reduce per-iteration overhead for RVV arraycopy stubs. The current implementation uses a single LMUL=m8 loop that calls `vsetvli` on every iteration, which adds unnecessary configuration overhead in the hot loop. pulls.title: 8381180: GenShen: Account for time required to independently execute each GC phase
pulls.author: kdnilsen
pulls.body_excerpt: The purpose of this PR is to individually model the time required to perform each phase of GC, specificially mark, evac, update, and final-roots. This allows us to more accurately predict the time that will be required to perform a GC operation. We maintain the existing mechanisms that predict typical GC times as an average and as a linear trend analysis of recently completed typical GC efforts. pulls.title: 8377154: AArch64: Merging SIMD ld/st into ldp/stp in macro-assembler
pulls.author: fg1417
pulls.body_excerpt: JDK-8196064 added support for merging 4- and 8-byte scalar load/store operations into load/store pairs. The AArch64 platform also supports SIMD load/store pairs for SIMD&FP registers[1]. This patch extends that functionality to support merging 4-, 8-, and 16-byte vector load/store operations into vector load/store pairs. For example, given the following assembly: ``` str q16, [x14, #32] str q16, [x14, #48] ``` after this change, it can be merged into: ``` stp q16, q16, [x14, #32] ``` Tier 1~3 tests passed on aarch64 platform.
